clue.text: Ballet in which ankle was twisted?

indicators.note: a twisted ankle is wrenched out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about which ballet saw a dancer suffer a sprained ankle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tchaikovsky's famous ballet about Odette, the princess turned into a bird, is a classic example of the art form.

clue.text: What's more severe, imprisoning king, civil engineer or magician?

indicators.note: imprisoning means the first word holds the others locked inside it

parts.note: sorer means more severe, as a sorer blow
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A riddle asking which is harsher: a jailed monarch, an engineer or a wizard.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorcerer is a wizard who works spells, a synonym for one who performs magic.

clue.text: Almost everything I have is in use

indicators.note: almost means the word stops just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: all means everything
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone claims nearly all their possessions are being put to work.
explanation.definitionFit: A system or idea that is still alive is active and current, still functioning in practice.

clue.text: Wink at something to have alternative appearance?

definitions.meaning: to wink at a misdeed is to pretend not to notice it
read literally, a look in a different direction: look as appearance, the other way as alternative

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: 'look' is an appearance and 'the other way' an alternative one.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore a wrongdoing deliberately is the idiomatic sense, just as winking at it means overlooking it.

clue.text: Expel king and recognise missing leader

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: missing leader means the phrase loses its first letter

parts.note: to pick out a face in a crowd is to recognise it

explanation.surface: A monarch is banished, and an acknowledged figurehead is absent.
explanation.definitionFit: To kick out is an informal synonym for eject or throw out of a place.

clue.text: Being handy, buys self-build in regular instalments

indicators.note: regular instalments means taking every other letter, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: A practical person buys a self-assembly kit and pays it off monthly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something handy is convenient and practical, which is a synonym for serviceable.

clue.text: Lack of internal clashes produces softness in cycle after agitation

indicators.note: agitation stirs things up, so the preceding words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A washing-machine cycle produces soft laundry once it has finished its agitating phase.
explanation.definitionFit: Being free of internal contradiction is precisely what logicians mean by an argument holding together coherently.

clue.text: Photography pioneer getting white robe for queen in dance

indicators.note: for means one piece stands in place of another within the word

parts.note: the foxtrot is a ballroom dance
R is short for regina, Latin for queen
an alb is a white vestment worn by priests

explanation.surface: A camera pioneer swaps a monarch for a priestly vestment on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: William Henry FOX TALBOT invented the calotype photographic process; ALB replaces the R in FOXTROT.
explanation.definitionFit: Fox Talbot was a nineteenth-century English inventor of early photographic methods, so a pioneer of the camera.

clue.text: Bays for manoeuvring with empty lorry?

definitions.text: Bays for manoeuvring with empty lorry?

indicators.note: manoeuvring means the letters are moved about into a new arrangement
empty means the word loses its contents, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Roadside spaces where a lorry with no load can pull in and turn.
explanation.walkthrough: An &lit: the whole clue describes roadside stopping bays, and also builds the answer from BAYS plus LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay-bys are roadside parking areas where lorries pull off the main carriageway.

clue.text: Terror intention is to be threatening

parts.note: a little terror is a mischievous child, an imp
an end is a goal or intention

explanation.surface: A terrorist's aim is to intimidate.
explanation.definitionFit: Danger that impends hangs over us menacingly, so is looming or about to strike.

clue.text: Large animal after rhesus monkey with lions' guts

parts.note: Rh is the abbreviation for rhesus, as in the blood factor

indicators.note: to monkey with something is to tamper with it, so these letters are mixed up
guts are the insides, so the middle letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: A big beast trails a rhesus monkey that is carrying lions' entrails.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhinoceros is a huge, horned, thick-skinned mammal, one of the largest land animals.

clue.text: Not simply former partner left in accord

indicators.note: in means these pieces are placed inside the word for accord

parts.note: to comply is to accord or conform
an ex is a former spouse or partner

explanation.surface: A divorce settlement was not straightforward, with the ex agreeing reluctantly.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in an intricate, complicated way is the opposite of doing it simply.

clue.text: Chosen people were transported by conductor

parts.note: the elect are those chosen, as by God
rode means travelled, were carried along

explanation.surface: A select group were carried along by a bus or train conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode is an electrical conductor through which current enters or leaves a circuit.

clue.text: Enthusiastic uproar about literal extremes

indicators.note: about means the first word surrounds the other

parts.note: a cry is an outcry or uproar
the letters at the extremes of the alphabet are A and Z

explanation.surface: A keen fan makes a fuss over taking words too literally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literal' here means 'of letters': the alphabet's extremes are A and Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Being crazy about something is an informal way of saying you are wildly keen on it.

clue.text: Art deserving and showing seriousness

definitions.meaning: in old English 'thou art deserving' is 'thou ...', from earn

explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' is the archaic verb of 'thou art'; the second-person form of earn takes the old -est ending.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest person is grave and sincere, demonstrating a serious intent.

clue.text: Waterway rising in Colorado and bridged by Rhode Island giant

parts.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island

indicators.note: bridged by means the word and is spanned, held inside the following pieces

parts.note: an ogre is a monstrous giant of folk tales

explanation.surface: A river that starts in Colorado is crossed by a huge structure from Rhode Island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rio Grande is a great North American river that has its source in the Colorado Rockies.

clue.text: Amateurish painter not quite capturing northern river

indicators.note: capturing means the shortened word takes the other letter inside it
not quite means the word stops one letter short

parts.note: a dauber is an unskilled painter

explanation.surface: A Sunday painter almost manages to paint a river in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danube is a major European river flowing from Germany to the Black Sea.

clue.text: Vituperate less at wild spouting

indicators.note: wild means the remaining letters are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: Abusing people less often, while gushing out wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' removes A and T from VITUPERATE, and 'wild' shuffles the rest, VIUPERTE.
explanation.definitionFit: An eruptive volcano or geyser is one that bursts out, spewing material forth.

clue.text: Little woman's story doesn't have a press

parts.note: Jo is one of the March sisters in Little Women, so Jo's

indicators.note: doesn't have means the letter is left out of the word

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A character from Little Women tells a tale without being pushy.
explanation.walkthrough: Jo March is the heroine of Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: To jostle is to push and shove against others, as a crowd presses forward.

clue.text: Vichy water not having a record year gets high praise

indicators.note: not having means the letter is removed from the word

parts.note: eau is French for water, Vichy being a French spa town
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: A spa water that has had no chart-topping year receives glowing reviews.
explanation.definitionFit: A eulogy is a speech or tribute of lavish commendation, often at a funeral.

clue.text: It's more sloshy?

indicators.note: sloshy suggests liquid sloshing about, so the letters are swilled into a new order

explanation.surface: A simple question about something being wetter.
explanation.walkthrough: An &lit: the words also say what the answer means, a thing that is wetter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wetter and more slushy is damper, the comparative of damp.

clue.text: French war minister against casually breaking his word

indicators.note: breaking means the second piece splits open the first

parts.note: mot is French for word, apt for a Frenchman
agin is a dialect or colloquial form of against

explanation.surface: A French minister breaks his promise by speaking against something offhandedly.
explanation.walkthrough: André MAGINOT, French minister of war, gave his name to the Maginot Line.
explanation.definitionFit: André Maginot was a French minister of war remembered for the defensive line built along the German border.

clue.text: Fear of enemy reported with endless prejudice

indicators.note: reported means the word is said out loud, giving its sound

parts.note: a foe is an enemy

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: bias means prejudice

explanation.surface: A dread of foes is said to come with unending bigotry.
explanation.definitionFit: A phobia is an irrational and intense dread of something.

clue.text: Nag has runs in stockings etc.

indicators.note: in means the letter is put inside the word

parts.note: hose is a collective term for stockings and tights
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone complains about ladders in their tights.
explanation.definitionFit: A nag is an old or worn-out riding animal, a colloquial term.

clue.text: Vessel illuminating dangers of sheep's lungs and haunch

parts.note: lights are the lungs of slaughtered animals, sold as offal
the haunch is the hip

explanation.surface: A ship's lantern is fuelled by mutton offal and a leg joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A lightship is a moored vessel bearing a beacon to warn mariners of hazards such as shoals.

clue.text: Writer using Nietzsche's seminal material?

indicators.note: using means the letters are drawn from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An author draws on Nietzsche's foundational ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: Hermann HESSE, German novelist, was strongly influenced by Nietzsche, so the surface is apt; 'material' is the stuff drawn on.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermann Hesse was a Nobel-winning German novelist, author of Steppenwolf.

clue.text: Popular movement to ostracise fwightful woman

parts.note: to ban someone is to exclude or ostracise them
a frightful woman is a dragon; the lisped spelling turns its R to W

explanation.surface: A craze for banning a scary woman, said with a childish lisp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fwightful' mimics a speaker who says W for R, so DRAGON becomes DWAGON.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandwagon is a fashionable cause or trend that many people jump on.

clue.text: Child of immigrants stays in bed, hiding head and turning over

indicators.note: turning over means the letters are read backwards
hiding head means the first letter is lost

parts.note: to lie in is to stay in bed late

explanation.surface: A second-generation child lies in late, burying their head under the covers and rolling over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding head' drops the L of LIESIN to leave IESIN, which 'turning over' turns into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nisei are American-born children of Japanese immigrant parents, second-generation citizens.

clue.text: With never a hint of sarcasm, say, sea's yes?

definitions.text: With never a hint of sarcasm, say, sea's yes?

parts.words: With never a hint of sarcasm, say, sea's yes?
parts.note: a sailor's reply of assent, the sincere seafaring cousin of a sarcastic 'yeah, yeah'

explanation.walkthrough: The surface contrasts a mocking 'yeah, yeah' with the naval acknowledgement of an order.
explanation.definitionFit: This doubled 'yes' is the traditional naval response confirming an order has been understood.

clue.text: Energy your old man's found with key natural gas product

parts.note: thy is the archaic form of your
Len is a man's name
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A father's power comes with a key to the gas works.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethylene is a hydrocarbon derived from natural gas and petroleum, used to make plastics.
